newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: INSIGHT-Aussie to test support as rally stalls.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Aussie to test support as rally stalls.

text.p: *AUD shade easier from Friday's late levels after a thin offshore session with bulls discouraged by failure at $0.7860
*Analysts not convinced uptrend in place despite rally from recent $0.7720 low and recommend jobbing the range for now
*Market cautious over RBA board meeting Tuesday, although no easing expected, and ahead of Macfarlane testimony on Thursday
By 8.15 am (2215 GMT) the local dollar had drifted to US$0.7818/23 from US$0.7831/36 late here Friday, but remained comfortably up on the US$0.7760/65 held this time last week.

Further support was put at US$0.7785, US$0.7760 and US$0.7735 while a major chart barrier lay ahead at US$0.7895/05, the capture of which would add a whole new sense of urgency to the uptrend and herald a rise to 80 cents.

On the crosses it eased to 99.00/10 yen from 99.12/22 but dealers expected further demand from Tokyo -- at least once today's Japanese holiday was over -- following last week's burst of interest in A$ bonds and dual currency samurais.

The revival in Japanese demand stemmed from a sharp widening in the A$'s yield premium over the US$ which in turn reflected a lessening in the risk of a rate cut here and a growing feeling U.S. rates would not have to rise as much as first feared.
Market confidence on domestic policy will be tested this week as the Reserve Bank board meets Tuesday and, were it to decide to ease, it would be expected to do so the day after.

Most felt the uncomfortably high 4.6 percent rise in Q1 weekly earnings reported last week would have tipped the balance against a move, but were wating to see what governor Ian Macfarlane said on Thursday before completely ruling out a cut.

This will be Macfarlance's first testimony on the course of monetary policy -- the Australian equivalent to Humphrey Hawkins -- to a Parliamentary committee and is eagerly awaited by a market starved of guidance on current policy thinking.
Also due Thursday are jobs data for April which could well swing sentiment back to an easing if they showed employment falling for the third month in a row.

Elsewhere, the dollar eased on sterling as the market looked for an early hike in U.K. rates following Labour's win. Traders said SBC had recommended selling A$ for sterling, but noted SBC had been bearish on the A$ for some time. -- Wayne Cole
